That which leads from its western side to the Elbe river is at 40 longitude and 52 2/3 latitude. The southern side, however, is bounded by the western part of the Danube river <note>original: "Danubij"</note>, so the head [source] of the Danube is at 30 longitude and 46 1/3 latitude. The part of the river that first branches toward Germany is at 32 longitude and 47 1/4 latitude. The second branching of the river, where it turns south and is called the Inn <note>original: "Enos"</note>, is at 34 longitude and 47 1/3 latitude. The branching of the second part of the river where it turns toward the north at the Gabreta Forest <note>original: "Goreta siluā"; the Bohemian Forest.</note> is at 36 longitude and 46 2/3 latitude. That which in the following branching at the Luna Forest <note>original: "luna siluam"</note> turns north is at 39 1/3 longitude and 47 1/2 latitude. The bend which then follows, from which it flows south, is at 40 2/3 longitude and 47 1/3 latitude. That which in the branching of the river flows south and is called the Naab <note>original: "Narabon"</note> is at 41 longitude and 47 1/3 latitude. The bend then following at the Capri, which is the most northern of all, is at 42 1/2 longitude and 48 latitude. 

The eastern side indeed limits the distance which is made from the aforementioned bend to the Sarmatian Mountains <note>The Carpathians.</note> which loom over it, the southern end of which has 42 1/2 degrees longitude and 48 degrees latitude. The northern end indeed is at 43 1/2 longitude and 50 1/2 latitude. Furthermore, there is the distance which is after the mountains to the said head of the Vistula river, and the river itself even as far as the sea. 

Of the mountains which surround Germany, the most well-known are those already mentioned and those properly called Sarmatian: and those having the same name as the Alps which are above the head of the Danube, the extremities of which have 29 & 47 and 33 & 48 1/2 degrees. Furthermore, those which are called Abnoba <note>The Black Forest mountains.</note>, the extremities of which have 31 longitude and 49 latitude and 31 longitude and 51 latitude. Also Mount Melibocus <note>Likely the Harz mountains.</note>, whose boundaries are 33 longitude and 52 1/2 latitude and 37 longitude and 52 1/2 latitude. Below these is the Semana Forest <note>The Thuringian Forest.</note>. And from there the Sudeti mountain <note>original: "sicurgius mons"; scribal variant for the Sudetes.</note> whose boundaries are 39 longitude and 54 latitude and 40 1/4 longitude and 53 1/2 latitude. Also the mountains called the Sudetes <note>original: "subdete"</note>, the extremities of which have 34 longitude and 50 latitude and 39 longitude and 50 latitude. Below these is the Gabreta Forest, the middle of which and of the Sarmatian Mountains is the Hercynian Forest <note>original: "orcyniū nemus"</note>. There inhabit Germany, around the Rhine river, starting from the northern part, those called the Lesser Bructeri <note>original: "Busactori parui"</note>, and the Sugambri, the Angrivarii <note>original: "Oquenj"</note>, and the Lombards <note>original: "longobardi"</note>. Afterward the Tencteri and the Nerteranes <note>original: "Tegatri & Nitriones"</note>.

-> # II. <note>This marks the second section of the description of Germany.</note> <-

Between the Rhine and the **Abnoba mountains** <note>original: "abnobos montes"; the Black Forest region in southwestern Germany.</note>. Furthermore, the Intuergi, the Vangiones, and the Caritni, below whom are the Vispi and the **Eleutiorian wilderness** <note>original: "eleutiorū eremus"; likely referring to an unpopulated or frontier region.</note>, extending as far as the aforementioned Alps. In the part along the ocean, the **Frisians** <note>original: "phrisij"</note> dwell above the Bructeri as far as the **Ems river** <note>original: "Amusiū fluuiū"</note>. After these are the **Chauci**, who are called the "Small Chauci," as far as the **Weser river** <note>original: "fluuiū visurgim"</note>. Then the so-called "Great Chauci" as far as the **Elbe river** <note>original: "albū fluuium"</note>. Then, above the neck of the **Cimbric Chersonese** <note>original: "Cymbrice Chersonesi"; the Jutland peninsula (modern Denmark).</note>, are the Saxons. Upon the Chersonese itself, above the Saxons to the west, dwell the Sigulones; then the Sabalingii; then the Cobandi; above whom are the Chali. Furthermore, above these, those who are further west are the Phundusii, and those further east are the Charudes. Of all these, the most northern are the **Cimbri**. After the Saxons, from the **Chalusus river** <note>Possibly the Trave or Warnow.</note> to the **Suevus river** <note>Usually identified as the Oder or the Swine.</note>, the Pharodini hold the land. After them, the Sidini as far as the **Viadrus river** <note>original: "Iduam"; likely the Oder.</note> are below them. Then the Rutidians as far as the **Vistula river** <note>original: "Istulam"</note>.

**The interior and inland parts are mostly held by:**
The **Suebic Angli** <note>original: "Sueui angili"; the Angles, who later migrated to Britain.</note>, who are further east than the **Lombards** <note>original: "longobardi"</note>, stretching north as far as the middle of the Elbe river. Toward the Suebi are the **Semnones**, who dwell beyond the Elbe from the aforementioned part toward the east as far as the Suevus river. Furthermore, they extend to the **Burgundians** <note>original: "Mugotas"; a transcription variant of Burgundi.</note> who hold the rest of the lands following from there as far as the Vistula. Among the minor tribes and those lying between the Small Chauci and the Suebi are the **Bructeri** (called the "Lesser"), below whom are the Chaemae. Between the Great Chauci and the Suebi lie the Angrivarii. After them are the Lombards, below whom are the Dulgubnii. Between the Saxons and the Suebi are the Tencteri and the Viruni. Between the Pharodini Suebi are the Teutons and Avars. Between the Rutidians and the Burgundians are the Helveconae. Again, below the Semnones dwell the Silingi. Below the Burgundians are the Lugi Omani. Below these are the Lugi Diduni as far as the **Asciburgium mountain**. Below the Silingi are the Calucones on either side of the Elbe. Below these are the Chaeruscans and the Great Chauci <note>Likely a scribal error for the Chamavi or similar inland tribe.</note> as far as the **Melibocus mountain**; to the east of these, around the Elbe river, the Bainochaemae hold the land; above whom are the Batini; above whom also, below the **Asciburgium mountain**, are the Corconti and the Lugi Buri as far as the head of the Vistula river. Below these, first are the Sidones. Then the Cotini. Then the Visurgii. After the **Hercynian Forest** <note>original: "orciniū nemus"; the vast ancient forest of central Germany.</note>, again from the rising of the Abnoba mountains, the Casuarii dwell below the Suebi. Then the Nerterane. Then the Danduti; below whom are the Turoni and Marvingi. Below the Chamavi are the Chattuarii and Tubanti, and above the Sudetic mountains are the Teuriochaemae. Below the mountains are the Varisti, then the **Gabreta Forest** <note>The Bohemian Forest.</note>. Below the Marvingi are the Curiones, then the Chaetaori, reaching as far as the **Danube river**. The Parmecampi are below the Gabreta Forest. The **Marcomanni** dwell below these, beneath whom are the Sudini, reaching as far as the Danube and the Adrobic plains. Below the Hercynian Forest are the **Quadi**, below whom are iron mines and the **Luna Forest**, below which is the great nation of the **Baemi** <note>original: "Bemoruz"; the Boii or people of Bohemia.</note> as far as the Danube, to whom the Catualda territory is contiguous along the river, as are the Rakatae plains.

# THE SITUATION OF RAETIA

**R** <note>ornamental initial with foliage</note> AETIA’S WESTERN side is bounded by Mount Adula <note>Likely the Saint-Gotthard Massif or the Splügen Pass region in the Central Alps.</note> and the line which runs between the heads of the rivers Rhine and Danube. Its northern side is bounded by a part of the Danube, which extends from its source to the fork of the river Inn <note>original: "eni fluuij"; the Inn River is a major tributary of the Danube.</note>, located at 34° 47 1/2'. Its eastern side is bounded by the Inn river itself, whose southern end is at 34° 49 1/4'. Its southern side is bounded by the Alpine mountains extending above Italy; on the Greek side, the coordinates are 30° 49 1/3'. Those near the Pennine Alps <note>original: "poenas"; referring to the Pennine range of the Alps.</note>, near the head of the Latius <note>likely the Lech</note> river which flows into the Danube and separates Raetia from Vindelicia, are at 31 1/2° 49 1/2'. Those at the furthest extent are at 33 1/3° 49 1/2'. The Brixantae inhabit the more northern parts of Raetia; the Suanetae and Rugusci inhabit the more southern parts. The Calucones and Vennontes occupy the regions between these.

# OF BOTH PANNONIAS

<margin>88.</margin>

...a parallel line: which from the aforementioned western boundary goes through the Alban mountain <note>The Mons Albanus, likely referring to the Hrušica plateau in modern Slovenia.</note> as far as the Bebian mountains <note>The Petrova Gora or Velebit range.</note> and the limits of Lower Pannonia, which have the coordinates 41 1/2° and 45 1/3°. To the north, it is bounded by the aforementioned mountain of Noricum <note>The Mons Cetius or Wienerwald.</note> and by that part of the Danube which runs from Mount Cetius to the mouth <note>original: "scillionē"; likely a corruption of "ostium" (mouth) or "scissionem" (splitting/fork).</note> of the Arabon river <note>The Raab River.</note>, which has coordinates 41° 47 1/3'. From the rising of the sun <note>From the East.</note>: by Lower Pannonia along a line having the aforementioned limits. The provinces are occupied in the northern part by the Azali <note>original: "zali"</note>, who are further west, and the Cytni <note>original: "Citi"</note>, who are further east. To the south are the Latobici, who are below Noricum, and toward the east the Varciani. Between them, toward the west, are the Boii <note>original: "Bij"</note>, and below them the Colapiani <note>original: "Coletiani"</note>; the Jasi <note>original: "Iassij"</note> are toward the east, and below them the Oseriates <note>original: "oderiaces"</note>.

# THE SITUATION OF LOWER PANNONIA

**P** <note>ornamental initial P</note> ANNONIA Lower is bounded on the west by Upper Pannonia, from the fork of the Arabon river according to the aforementioned limits. To the south is a part of Illyricum, which from the said limit extends as far as the flow of the Danube where the Sava river <note>original: "Sauus"</note> branches off, the coordinates of which are 45° 44 1/2'. To the north and east it is bounded by the part of the Danube which runs from the fork of the Arabon river to the Sava river, and it has its location here after the Arabon river. The bend which occurs near Curta is 42° 47'. The most northern part of the Danube, which flows through the two Pannonias, splits at the city of Carrodunum toward Mount Cetius, near its northernmost parts which are called Sabaria, and toward the south.
| Name | Longitude | Latitude |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| Daros | 44 1/2 | 45 1/3 |

**The turning of the same Danube near Cornacum is 45° 45 1/3'**
**The joining <note>original: "conūlio"; likely 'conuulsio' or 'confluuio'</note> of the same near Ruttium is 45 1/2° 45'**
**Which is near the fork of the Sava river, which itself extends through the two Pannonias and joins Mount Cetius; first toward the north and later toward the west at 45° 44 1/2'**
Furthermore, they occupy this province: in the western parts, the Amantini are more northern; below whom are the Heruniates. After them are the Andizetes <note>original: "andiantes"</note>. Then the Breuci. In the eastern parts: those who are most northern are the Eravisci <note>original: "Arauisci"</note>; and those further south are the Scordisci.

### THE SITUATION OF ILLYRIS, OR LIBURNIA, OR DALMATIA
[[margin: 88.]]
ILLYRIS is bounded [Note: *tñiatur* expanded to *terminatur*] on the northern side by both Pannonias along the set mountains. On the west by Istria along a line whose degree is held toward the end of Upper Pannonia at 36 1/2 [longitude] 45 1/6 [latitude]. But the end [Note: *Fiuis* likely error for *Finis*] which is in the Adriatic gulf is at 36 1/2 44 2/3 1/3. On the east by Upper Moesia along a line which [Note: *ꝙ* expanded to *quod*] extends from the said division of the river Savus [Sava] as far as the end which is near Mount Sardonius, the degrees of which are 47 41 1/3. # BOOK THREE OF THE COSMOGRAPHY OF CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY CONTAINS
The exposition of the eastern part of Europe according to the subject provinces or satrapies: all of Italy, the island of Cyrnus [Corsica], the island of Sardinia, the island of Sicily, European Sarmatia, the Tauric Chersonese [Crimea], the Iaziges Metanastae, Dacia, Upper Moesia, Lower Moesia, the Thracian Chersonese, Macedonia, Epirus, Achaia, Peloponnesus, the island of Euboea, and the island of Crete.

### THE SITUATION OF ITALY
[[margin: 90. 94.]]
ITALY HAS its boundaries on the west at the ridges of the Alps along a line which [Note: *ꝙ* expanded to *quod*] extends from Mount Adula as far as the mouths of the river Varus, the degrees of which are 27 1/2 43. Furthermore, the shore of the Tyrrhenian Sea from Neapolis, namely, as far as Leucopetra. On the north it is bounded by the ridges of the Alps which overhang Raetia. Furthermore, by the Peonis and Ocra and Mount Caruadius which is below Noricum, the degrees of which have been stated. Besides this, by the shore of the Adriatic gulf from the river Lananpus as far as Mount Garganus and Hydruntum. On the south: by the shore of the Adriatic Sea from the river Lauampus as far as the Illyrian boundary. Furthermore, by the Ligurian and Tyrrhenian shore from the mouths of the Varus, namely, as far as Neapolis, and from Leucopetra as far as Hydruntum. It is described in this manner after the mouths of the river Varus in the Ligurian Sea.

### THE SITUATION OF THE ISLAND OF SICILY
[[margin: 92.]]

## THE SITUATION OF EUROPEAN SARMATIA

[[Historiated initial 'S' depicting a dragon or serpent in a landscape.]]

**S**ARMATIA OF EUROPE [abbrev: *EVROpe* → *EUROPAE*] is bounded on the north by the Sarmatian ocean near the Venedic gulf, and by a part of the unknown land according [abbrev: *scđm* → *secundum*] to this description. After the mouths of the Vistula [abbrev: *istale* → *Vistulae*] river: [abbrev: *ff* → *fluvii*]

| | Longitude | Latitude |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

The position of the shore which [abbrev: *ꝙ* → *quod*] is marked through [abbrev: *ꝑ* → *per*] the parallel of the island of Thule: this is the limit of the sea of the known land: 62 [long.] 63 [lat.]
The limit near the southern region of Sarmatia which [abbrev: *ꝙ* → *quod*] is described through [abbrev: *ꝑ* → *per*] the sources of the Tanais has [abbrev: *gđ⁹* → *gradus*] degrees 64 [long.] 63 [lat.] and 64 [long.] 68 [lat.]

From the west it is bounded by the Vistula river and the part of Germany which is between its head and the Sarmatian mountains. Moreover, by those mountains themselves whose degrees have been stated. From the south by the Iazyges Metanastae. From the southern limit of the Sarmatian mountains as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ* → *usque*] the beginning of the Carpathian mountain, which [abbrev: *ꝙ* → *quod*] has degrees 46 [long.] 48 1/2 [lat.]. Moreover, continuously through [abbrev: *ꝑ* → *per*] Dacia along the same parallel as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ* → *usque*] the mouths of the Borysthenes river [abbrev: *ff* → *fluminis*]. And from here by the Pontic shore as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ* → *usque*] the Carcinitus river.

## SITUATION OF DACIA

[[Historiated initial 'D' depicting a figure or landscape within.]]

**D**ACIA is bounded on the north
by the part [abbrev: *pte*] of Sarmatia
of Europe, namely from the Car-
pathian mountain as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ*] the end
of the aforesaid bend of the Tyra
river: the degrees of which are
as has been said 49 49 1/2
On the west by the Iazyges Metanastae along the Tibiscus stream; on the south as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ*] the Danube from the split of the Tibiscus river as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ*] to Axium of the Danube, a city from which the Danube as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ*] the Pontus and the mouths is called the Ister. The situation of this part is as follows. After the split of the Tibiscus river, the first bend to the south: 47 2/3 [long.] 44 2/4 [lat.].
Split of the Catarabo river [abbrev: *ff*] which is carried to Dacia: 49 [long.] 43 1/2 [lat.].

The bend near Osceum: 51 [long.] 44 [lat.].
The bend near the city of Axium: 54 2/3 [long.] 44 2/4 [lat.].
From here the Danube as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ*] the mouths, as we said above, is called the Ister. On the east, however, it is bounded then by the Ister river as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ*] the bend which is near the city of Dinogetia, the degrees of which are 53 [long.] 46 2/3 [lat.].
Moreover, it is bounded by the Hierasus river: which [abbrev: *ꝙ*], split from the Ister near Dinogetia, is carried to the north and east as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ*] the aforesaid bend of the Tyra river as has been said, of degrees 53 [long.] 48 1/2 [lat.].
The Anarti and Teurisci hold the most northern part of Dacia from the western region: and the Coertoboci; and below these the Predasensii: and the Racatensii and the Caucoensii. has degrees 55 44 1/3. From the north through [abbrev: *ꝑ*] the aforesaid limits of the Ciabrus river and the Danube as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ*] to the city of Axium and then from the Danube called the Ister: as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ*] its mouths which [abbrev: *ꝙ*] go out into the Pontus. Its bend indeed near the city of Dinogetia is said to have degrees 53 [long.] 46 1/3 [lat.].
The mouths truly have themselves in this order. The first section of them which [abbrev: *ꝙ*] is near the city of Iodunum has degrees 54 1/2 1/3 and 46 1/2. From there, the part which is furthest south, encircling the island called Peuce, has degrees 55 1/3 [long.] 46 1/2 [lat.]. It exits into the Pontus by the mouth which is called the Sacred Peuce at degrees 56 46 1/4. The part of it which [abbrev: *ꝙ*] turns most to the north is itself split near degrees 55 46 1/2 1/4. The most northern part of this section rests a little before its exit into the Pontus. It forms a marsh by the name of Thyagola: the more northern parts of which have degrees 55 1/3 and 47 1/4. It then exits into the Pontus by a thin mouth which they also call Thyagola at degrees 56 1/4 47. The more southern part of the second section is itself split in degrees 55 1/3 46 1/2 1/4. And that which [abbrev: *qđ*] turns more to the north of this section exits into the Pontus by the mouth which is called Boreum, whose degrees are 56 1/2 46 1/2 1/3. The more southern part however is itself divided at degrees 55 46 1/2 and the more southern part of this exits into the Pontus by the mouth which is named Tinariatium, whose degrees are 56 2/3 46 1/3. The part which is more northern is itself split near degrees 56 46 2/3. And that which [abbrev: *qđ*] turns most to the north of this section exits by the mouth called Pseudostomium at degrees 56 1/4 46 3/4. That which truly is more southern exits by the mouth which is called Calostomium, whose degrees are 56 1/4 46 1/2. The eastern part however of Moesia is bounded then by the shore of the Pontus: as far as [abbrev: *vſꝙ*] the aforesaid limit of Thrace, which has degrees 55 2/3 44 1/3. ## LOCATION OF THE IAZYGES METANASTAE

[[image: Historiated initial 'I' depicting flowers.]]

**T**HE IAZYGES METANASTAE <note>The "Migrant" Iazyges, a Sarmatian tribe that moved into the plains of modern-day Hungary.</note> have as their borders to the north European Sarmatia—specifically that part of Sarmatia which is south of the Sarmatian mountains—as far as the Carpathian mountain. To the west and south, they are bordered by the aforementioned part of Germany <note>Ptolemy is referring to his previous descriptions of the Germanic borders.</note>, stretching from the Sarmatian mountains to the Carpathian mountain and the bend of the Danube river, up to the split of the Tibiscus river <note>The Tisza River.</note>, which flows to the north <note>original: "arctum"</note> at 46 [long.] and 44 1/4 [lat.].
To the east, they are bordered by Dacia along the same Tibiscus river, which turns toward the east <note>original: "ortum"</note> below the Carpathian mountain; at this point, the degrees are 46 [long.] and 48 [lat.].

The cities of the Iazyges are these:

## LOCATION OF DACIA

[[image: Historiated initial 'D' depicting a figure or landscape within.]]

**D**ACIA is bounded on the north by a part of European Sarmatia, from the Carpathian mountain to the end of the previously mentioned bend of the Tyras river <note>The Dniester River.</note>; the degrees of which are, as stated, 49 [long.] and 49 1/2 [lat.].
To the west, it is bounded by the Iazyges Metanastae along the Tibiscus river. To the south, it extends as far as the Danube, from the separation of the Tibiscus river to the city of Axius on the Danube, from which point the Danube is called the Ister <note>The Romans often called the upper part the Danubius and the lower part the Ister.</note> as far as the Black Sea and its mouths. The location of this part is as follows: after the separation of the Tibiscus river, the first bend to the south is at 47 2/3 [long.] 44 2/4 [lat.].
The separation of the Catarabonis river, which is carried toward Dacia: 49 [long.] 43 1/2 [lat.].
The part which is near the separation of the Aluta river <note>The Olt River in Romania.</note>, which is carried toward the north with great force and divides Dacia: 50 [long.] 44 [lat.].
The bend near Osceum: 51 [long.] 44 [lat.].
The bend near the city of Axius: 54 2/3 [long.] 44 2/4 [lat.].
From here, the Danube is called the Ister as far as its mouths, as we said above. To the east, it is bounded from the Ister river as far as the bend near the city of Diogetia, the degrees of which are 53 [long.] 46 2/3 [lat.].
Furthermore, it is bounded by the Hierasus river <note>The Siret River.</note>, which, split from the Ister near Diogetia, is carried to the north and east as far as the aforementioned bend of the Tyras river, as was said, at 53 [long.] 48 1/2 [lat.].
In the northernmost part of Dacia, the Anarti and Teurisci hold the western region, along with the Coertoboci; below these are the Predasensii, the Racatensii, and the Caucoensii. Below these similarly are the Biephi, the Buredacensii, and the Accotensii; and furthermore, below these are the Albocensii, the Potulatensii, and the Selsii. Below whom...

## THE LOCATION OF UPPER MOESIA

[[image: Historiated initial 'M' (or decorated pattern).]]

**U**PPER MOESIA <note>A Roman province situated in the central Balkans, mainly in modern-day Serbia.</note> is bounded to the west by Dalmatia along the previously mentioned line: specifically from the branch of the Savus <note>The Sava River.</note> as far as Mount Scardus. From there, to the south, it extends as far as Macedonia through Mount Orbelus to the boundary located at coordinates 49 [longitude] 42 1/2 [latitude]. To the east lies a part of Thrace: which extends from the aforementioned boundary to the river Ciabrus <note>The modern Tsibritsa River in Bulgaria.</note> near the terminus of which the coordinates are 50 43. Furthermore, the river Ciabrus itself runs alongside Lower Moesia until the point where the Ciabrus flows into the Danube, where the coordinates are 49 1/2 45 1/2. From there, to the north, it is bounded by the part of the Danube as far as the river Savus. The Triconensii occupy the province near Dalmatia. Those peoples who are along the Ciabrus are the Moesians, and those who lie between them are the Picensii. Those who are near Macedonia are the Dardani <note>The Dardani were a significant tribe whose territory covered parts of modern Kosovo, Serbia, and North Macedonia.</note>.

it has coordinates of 55° [longitude] and 44 1/3° [latitude]. From the north, it is bounded by the borders of the Ciabrus River <note>The Ciabrus is the modern Tsibritsa River in Bulgaria.</note> and the Danube, as far as the city of Axius, and from there by the Danube, which is also called the Ister <note>original: "Danubrio Istro appellato"; the Greeks and Romans typically called the lower part of the Danube the Ister.</note>, as far as its mouths which empty into the Euxine Sea <note>The Black Sea.</note>. Its bend near the city called Diogenia is said to have coordinates of 53° 46 1/3°. The mouths themselves are arranged in this order: the first section, which is near the city of Iodunum, is at 54 1/2 1/3° and 46 1/2°. From there, the most southern part, encircling the island called Peuce, is at 55 1/3° 46 1/2°. It exits into the sea at the mouth called the Sacred Mouth of Peuce <note>original: "Sacra peuca"</note> at 56° 46 1/4°. The part that turns most toward the north is itself split at 55° 46 1/2 1/4°. The northernmost part of this section rests a little before its exit into the sea, forming a marsh named Thyagola; its northern parts are at 55 1/3° and 47 1/4°. It then exits into the sea through a narrow mouth which they also call Thyagola at 56 1/4° 47°. The more southern part of the second section is itself split at 55 1/3° 46 1/2 1/4°. The part of this section that turns more toward the north exits into the sea at the mouth called the Northern Mouth <note>original: "boreum"</note>, at 56 1/2° 46 1/2 1/3°. The more southern part is also divided at 55° 46 1/2°, and the southern portion of this exits into the sea at the mouth named Tinariatium at 56 2/3° 46 1/3°. The northern part is also split at 56° 46 2/3°. The part of this section that turns most toward the north exits at the mouth called the False Mouth <note>original: "pseudostomio"</note> at 56 1/4° 46 3/4°. The more southern part exits at the mouth called the Beautiful Mouth <note>original: "Calstomium"</note> at 56 1/4° 46 1/2°. The eastern part of Moesia is bounded by the shore of the sea, as far as the previously mentioned border of Thrace, which is at 55 2/3° 44 1/3°. ## THE LOCATION OF THRACE

[[image: Historiated initial 'T' showing figures within the letter, likely representing scholars or provincial personifications.]]

**T**HRACE is bounded on the north by Lower Moesia along the previously described line. From the west, it is bounded by Upper Moesia and part of Macedonia, specifically from the aforementioned Mount Orbelus to the boundary located at 49° [longitude] and 42 1/2° [latitude]. To the south, it is bounded by the part of Macedonia from the aforementioned boundary to the mouth of the Nessus river <note>The Mesta River in modern Bulgaria and Greece.</note>, extending through the Aegean Sea and part of the Melas Gulf <note>The "Black Gulf," now the Gulf of Saros.</note> and the line that divides the Chersonese <note>The Gallipoli Peninsula.</note>. ## DESCRIPTION OF EPIRUS

[[image: Historiated initial 'P' depicting a figure.]] <note>A historiated initial is an enlarged letter at the start of a chapter containing a picture. Though the letter is 'P', it serves as the first letter of 'Epiri' (Epirus) in this context.</note>

**E**PIRUS is bounded on its most northern side by part of Macedonia, according to the line already described. This translation follows scholarly standards for Renaissance Latin, specifically a 15th-century printed edition of Ptolemy’s *Cosmographia*. 

**Translation Notes:**
*   **Proper Nouns:** As requested, Latin forms of geographical names (cities, rivers, mountains) have been retained.
*   **Abbreviations:** Common abbreviations expanded: *ff.* = *fluminis* (of the river); *pmontoriū/promonto.* = *promontorium* (promontory/cape); *mō.* = *mons/monte* (mountain); *p̃fatis/p̄dicta* = *praefatis/praedicta* (aforementioned); *q̃/ꝙ* = *quod/que* (which/and); *ostia* = river mouths.
*   **Coordinates:** Ptolemaic coordinates are expressed in degrees and fractions of degrees (e.g., 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/12). These have been transcribed exactly as they appear.

### . III . [BOOK III]
### THE SITUATION OF ACHAIA OR HELLAS
[Woodcut initial 'A']

**ACHAIA, which is joined to the aforementioned regions as far as the Peloponnesian river Ischinum, which they also call Hellada: its boundaries are, from the west, Epyrus; from the north, Macedonia, along the predicted sides and part of the Aegean Sea; from the east (the rising sun), then by part of the Aegean Sea as far as the Sunium promontorium. From the south, the Adriatic Sea along the coast, which extends from the Acheloo river to the Corinthian Gulf; and hence the Ischinum [Isthmus]; and hence the Cretan sea as far as the Sunium promontorium. And this is the description of the coast. After the Acheloo river, which is the boundary of Epyri in the Adriatic Sea, the Ecole chersonesi promontorio [promontory of the Ecole peninsula].**

**THE THIRD BOOK OF THE COSMOGRAPHY OF CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY ENDS**

**THE FOURTH BOOK OF THE COSMOGRAPHY OF CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY, A MAN OF ALEXANDRIA, CONTAINS:**
An exposition of all Africa: according to the provinces or satrapies <note>A "satrapy" was an administrative province, a term originally used in the Persian Empire but adopted here by Ptolemy for regional divisions.</note> listed below: Mauretania Tingitana; Mauretania Caesariensis; Numidia; Africa; Cyrenaica; Marmarica; Libya; the whole of Egypt, both Lower and Upper; Interior Libya under the aforementioned provinces; and Ethiopia which is below Egypt.

### DESCRIPTION OF MAURITANIA CAESARIENSIS

This text appears to be a section from a Renaissance-era edition of Claudius Ptolemy’s *Geographia* (likely the Latin translation by Jacobus Angelus, often revised in the 15th and 16th centuries). It lists coordinates (longitude and latitude) for various locations in North Africa, Egypt, and Ethiopia.

### Translation Notes:
*   **Proper Nouns:** Following your instructions, these have been kept in their Latin forms (e.g., *Adrumanto* for Hadrumetum).
*   **Abbreviations/OCR Errors:** 
    *   The word **"be"** frequently appears where **"hae"** (these) is expected (e.g., *Insule aut libie adiacent... be* for *hae*).
    *   **"pua"** is a common OCR error for **"parva"** (small).
    *   **"aut"** is often an abbreviation for **"autem"** (however/moreover).
    *   **"salutariū"** with a tilde represents **"salutarium."**
*   **Coordinates:** The numbers represent degrees and fractions of degrees (1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/6, 1/12).
*   **Nomi:** Translated as "Nomes" (the traditional administrative districts of Egypt).

And the Nubi who hold the western parts of the valley of the mountain itself. And the Derbieci who turn more to the west than Mount Aranga. Afterwards toward it the Babii & Malcie & Mandori as far as the Doradas. Moreover below Mount Usagala are the Suburpotes; below Mount Girgiri, just as above the Garamantes, are the Maccoi and Daufice and Calcite as far as the Nuba marsh. Afterwards, east of the Daradis are the Machureti: and also between Mount Ocopha and the Chariot of the Gods they hold the Ophreis, under which are the Tarualte & Matite & the Affricerones, a great nation. Again, south of the Odrangili are the Archeme and for the Mimaces, the Gongale. After whom are the Canubis. Afterwards the Naubrate as far as Mount Arnaltum. Moreover between the marsh of Libya & the Tala mountains are the Alttambi & Maurali. And between these & the Nubi are the Armie & Thale and the Dolopes & Astacuri as far as the valley of the mountain. And more northern than Mount Aranca are the Arunce. Moreover further east are the Afarace. Moreover between the Derbici and Mount Arualtem are the Dormeneis and below the Africerones as if toward the south are the Agangine Ethiopians: to whom further east under the Mount Aruala itself as far as Mount Arangam are the Xileis Ethiopians. After whom are the Calceis Ethiopians.

## OF EGYPT AND MARMARICA

**M**armarica, together with Egypt, is bordered on the west by Cyrenaica along a line that extends through the city of Dardanis and part of inner Libya toward that same southern limit, the degree of which is 51 1/4 23. From the north, it is bordered by the Egyptian Sea according to this description of the coast of the Prefecture of Marmarica or its <term>Nomes</term> <note>Nomes were the traditional administrative districts of ancient Egypt.</note>.

<margin>¶ The Nile itself and the Nomes <note>A "Nome" (from the Greek 'nomos') was an administrative subdivision or province of ancient Egypt.</note> which are around it.</margin>

<margin>¶ Furthermore, the more notable cities are situated as follows.</margin>

<margin>¶</margin> That which is called the **Great Delta** is the area where the river called the *Agathos Daimon* <note>original: "Agathos demon" — Greek for "Good Spirit." This refers to the westernmost Canopic branch of the Nile.</note> is divided; this branch flows through the Heracleotic mouth into the river called the Bubastic, which in turn flows out through the Pelusiac mouth. The position of this split at the Delta is 62 30. It is also called the **Small Delta**, where the Bubastic river is divided, flowing into the Busiritic river which runs out through the Pathmetic mouth; the Small Delta is at 62 1/3 30 1/3. There could also be named a **Third Delta**, distinct from the aforementioned, where the Bubastic river is divided, running through the city of Athribis and exiting through the Pineptimi mouth; the coordinates of this third Delta are 62 1/4 30 1/12. Near the Great Delta, a branch is led off from the *Agathos Daimon* river toward the north; this is the first branch, called the Phermuthiac river, which flows through the Sebennytic mouth, and its diversion point is at 61 1/2 30 1/4. Then there is a second such river which exits through the Bolbitine mouth, and its diversion point is at 61 30 1/2 1/3. From there, both rivers join near almost the same parallel of the shore: the Phermuthiac, the Athribitic, the Busiric, and the Bubastic rivers, from which some exit to the sea through the waves and marshes, while others, through the remaining mouths, mingle with the aforementioned great rivers.

<margin>¶</margin> The region around these rivers is called by the common name: the **Lower Region** <note>Referring to Lower Egypt, the northern part of the country encompassing the Delta.</note>.

-> <margin>¶</margin> **DESCRIPTION OF INLAND LIBYA** <margin>¶</margin> <-

<image-desc>A large historiated initial 'L' set in a square frame. The letter is blue with white vine-work patterns, set against a gold leaf background. **Inland Libya** is bounded on the north by the two Mauritanias <note>Mauritania Tingitana and Mauritania Caesariensis.</note>, by Africa, and by Cyrene along the southern lines already described. From the rising sun (the east), it is bounded by part of Marmarica along the meridian of the city of Dardanis, up to the previously described border of Marmarica; and furthermore by Ethiopia which is below Egypt, extending from that same southern point to its end, the position of which is 51 1/4 longitude and 23 1/6 latitude. On the south, it is bounded by Lower Ethiopia, in which is the region of Agisymba <note>A vast territory in central Africa mentioned by Ptolemy, representing the southern limit of the known world.</note>, along a line that extends from the aforementioned end to the western limit called the Great Hesperian Gulf of the Inland Sea, the position of which is 14 1/4 longitude and 4 latitude. On the west, it is bounded by the Western Ocean from the aforementioned gulf to the border of Tingitana Mauritania. Its coastline, along with the part of Tingitana Mauritania, is as follows:

### THE POSITION OF INTERIOR ETHIOPIA

[[image: Decorative initial 'V' showing a sphere/globe with stylized continents and foliage patterns.]]

BELOW <note>The Latin 'VE' is likely a decorative abbreviation or a transcription of 'Sub', meaning 'Below'</note> this region and all of Libya lies Ethiopia. It is bounded on the north by the southern lines of the aforementioned regions, specifically from the Great Gulf of the Outer Sea <note>The Atlantic Ocean</note> as far as the promontory of Raptum <note>original: "Raptu promontorium," likely located near modern-day Tanzania</note>, which has coordinates of 71 1/2 1/3 degrees [longitude] and 8 1/2 1/12 southern [latitude]. Furthermore, part of the Indian Ocean near the Great Gulf is bounded on the west and south by Unknown Land <note>original: "terra incognita"</note>. To the east, it is bounded by the Barbarian Gulf, which is called the "Brene" sea, extending from the promontory of Raptum to the promontory of Prassum, and from there to the Unknown Land. The promontory of Prassum has coordinates of 80 degrees [longitude] and 15 southern [latitude], near which, towards the summer rising of the sun <note>the North-East</note>, lies an island named Menuchias <note>possibly Zanzibar or Mafia Island</note> at 85 degrees [longitude] and 12 1/2 southern [latitude]. Now, around the gulf dwell the Ethiopian Cannibals <note>original: "Anthropophagi"</note>; to their west rise the Mountains of the Moon <note>original: "lune montes," famously thought by ancients to be the source of the Nile</note>, from which the marshes of the Nile receive their snows. Its borders have coordinates of 57 degrees [longitude], 12 1/2 southern [latitude] and 67 degrees [longitude], 12 1/2 southern [latitude]. Above these are the Repsi Ethiopians. Around the Great Gulf, which is by the Western Ocean, dwell the Ethiopian Fish-eaters <note>original: "Ichtrophagi"</note>, and further south of these as far as the Unknown Land are those commonly called the Hesperian <note>Western</note> Ethiopians. More to the east are the Anthace Ethiopians. Still further toward the east, next to all of Libya, is a great region of Ethiopians in which there are white elephants, rhinoceroses, and tigers. Next to the Unknown Land is a region of Ethiopians extending nearby called Agisymba. The region has many other great features reaching as far as the Unknown Land which have come to our knowledge; they are as follows:

Mount Dauchis, the middle of which is 15 [longitude], 13 southern [latitude]
Mount Ius, the middle of which is 10 [longitude], 8 1/3 1/12 southern [latitude]
Mount Ziphe, the middle of which is 25 [longitude], 8 1/3 1/12 southern [latitude]
Mount Melsbe, the middle of which is 25 [longitude], 13 southern [latitude]
Mount Barditi, the middle of which is 45 [longitude], 16 southern [latitude]

For from the southern part of our habitable world to the South Pole, there are 73 1/2 degrees, or 74 full degrees.

THE FOURTH BOOK OF THE COSMOGRAPHY OF CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY ENDS

THE FIFTH BOOK OF THE COSMOGRAPHY OF CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY, MAN OF ALEXANDRIA, BEGINS

An exposition of the first parts of Greater Asia: Pontus and Bithynia; the region properly called Asia; Phrygia; Lycia; Galatia; Paphlagonia; Cappadocia; Little Armenia; Cilicia; Asiatic Sarmatia; Colchis; Iberia; Albania; Greater Armenia; the island of Cyprus; Syria; Phoenicia; Palestine and Judea; Stony Arabia; Mesopotamia; Desert Arabia; Babylonia.

THE FIFTH BOOK BEGINS: THE POSITION OF PONTUS AND BITHYNIA

[[image: Decorative initial 'P' with floral motifs.]]

PONTUS AND BITHYNIA are bounded on the west by the mouth of the Pontus <note>The Black Sea</note>, the Thracian Bosphorus, and part of the Propontis <note>The Sea of Marmara</note>, according to this description of the Bithynian coast. In the mouth of the Pontus is the Temple of Diana.

To the south, it is bounded by the region properly called Asia and a line drawn from the Rhyndacus River as far as its end, which is positioned at 61 [longitude] 41 1/4 [latitude]. To the east <note>original: "ab ortu," literally from the rising sun</note> lies Galatia near Paphlagonia, along a line extending from the aforementioned end at 61 [longitude] 41 1/4 [latitude] to the recited city of the Pontus.

The more notable mountains in this region are Mount Orminius, the center of which is at 59 1/3 42 1/3, and Mount Olympus of Mysia at 57 43 1/2. The Chalcedonians <note>original: "charchedonij"</note> occupy the coast from the mouth to the Hyptius River. The Mariandyni occupy the coast from the city of Heraclea to the city of Cytorus. Below Mount Orminius are the Cyclones, and below the Chalcedonians extends the region of Semonitis, and below this the Bogdomanis, in which the Zigiani dwell toward the east.

### THE POSITION OF THE REGION PROPERLY CALLED ASIA MINOR <note>This refers to the Roman Province of Asia, comprising the western part of the Anatolian peninsula</note>

[[image: Decorative initial 'R' with floral patterns.]]

THE REGION which is properly called Asia is bounded on the north by Bithynia along the line described above. On the west, it is bounded by the remaining part of the Propontis <note>The Sea of Marmara</note>, the Hellespont, and the Aegean, Carian, and Myrtian seas according to this description of the coast of the Propontis of Lesser Mysia, which overlooks the Hellespont.

### DESCRIPTION OF LYCIA

<note>The following section begins with a large decorative initial 'L' adorned with swirling vine-like patterns.</note>

LYCIA is bounded on the west and north by Asia Minor along the lines already described; on the east by part of Pamphylia, extending from the border of Asia to the sea through Mount Massicytus <note>Original: "Masititu"</note>. The end of this boundary at the sea is at coordinates 61 1/2 1/3 [longitude] and 36 1/2 [latitude]. On the south, it is bounded by the Lycian Sea according to this description of the coast following Caunus:

### THE SITUATION OF GALATIA

[[image: Decorative initial 'G' with bird and leaf motifs.]]

GALATIA is bounded on the west by Bithynia and the part of Asia <note>Referring to the Roman Province of Asia</note> along the line already described. To the south, it borders Pamphylia from the aforementioned boundary of Asia as far as the point which, along the parallel, has the coordinates 64 1/3 38 1/2 1/12 43 1/6. To the east, it is bounded by the part of Cappadocia that extends from this limit to the Pontic Sea <note>The Black Sea</note> at the coordinates 65 2/4 43 1/6. To the north, it is bounded by the part of the Pontic Sea according to this description: after the coastal city of Cytorus.

### THE POSITION OF CAPPADOCIA

[[image: Decorative initial 'C' with floral designs.]]

CAPPADOCIA is bounded on the west by Galatia and part of Pamphylia along the line already described, from the Black Sea <note>Original: "ponto"</note> to the end, the coordinates of which are 64° 37 3/4'. To the south, it is bounded by Cilicia along the line that extends from there through Mount Taurus to its end at 70° 37 1/3'. Beyond that, it is bounded by the part of Syria that then runs along Mount Amanus <note>A mountain range in south-central Turkey, separating Cilicia from Syria</note> above the part of the Euphrates at 71 1/3° 38'. To the east, it borders Greater Armenia along the Euphrates, from the aforementioned part of Mount Amanus to the turn that is furthest north toward the sunrise <note>The northeast</note>, located at 72° 42 1/2'. Afterward, the boundary follows the line that extends along the mountains of the Molcori to the end at 72 3/4° 44 1/2' 1/4", and the line which joins from there to the predicted limit. To the north, it is bounded by the part of the Black Sea <note>Original: "ponti Euxini"</note> that stretches from Amisus in Galatia to the end at 72 3/4° 44 1/4'. The description of the coast of that part is as follows:

### THE SITUATION OF CILICIA
CILICIA is bounded on the west by the part of Pamphylia [already] set forth; on the east by the part of Mount Amanus which extends from the border of the Cappadocians as far as the boundary which is next to the Issic Gulf and as far as the Gates of Amanus. The degrees of this boundary are 69 $1/2$ 36 $1/2$ $1/3$. On the north by the part of Cappadocia set forth near Mount Taurus. On the south by the straits of Cilicia and the Issic Gulf; according to the description it holds itself thus. After the city of Sildra in Pamphylia, on the shore which follows, [is] the Trachean—that is, the rugged region—of Leontis.

### SITUATION OF GREATER ARMENIA
GREATER ARMENIA is bounded on the north by the part of Colchis and Iberia and Albania next to the line set forth along the Cyr river. On the west by the part of Cappadocia: according to the set line of the Sea of the Cappadocians as far as Colchis through the Moschici mountains. On the east by the part of the Hyrcanian Sea which extends from the mouths of the Cyr river as far as the border whose degrees are 79 $1/2$ $1/4$ 43 $1/3$. Moreover, by the Medes next to the line delivered over the Caspian mountain whose borders have degrees 79 42 $1/2$ and 80 $1/2$ 40. On the south by the part of Mesopotamia next to the line of Mount Taurus: which indeed is joined to the Euphrates river at degrees 71 $1/2$ 37 $1/3$. At the Tigris river indeed according to the situation having degrees 74 $1/2$ 38 $1/2$. ### SITUATION OF ARABIA PETRAEA
ARABIA PETRAEA is bounded on the west by the exposed part of Syria: on the north by Palestine Judea and a part of Syria next to the noted lines of them: on the south by the inner gulf of the Arabian Sea which has degrees 63 $1/2$ 29 $1/2$ $1/3$ and by the gulf near Hieropolis from the noted border at Egypt: as far as the promontory which is near Pharna and has degrees: 65 29. The villa of Elana indeed which is next to the gulf of the same name has degrees 65 $2/3$ $1/6$ 29 $1/4$. On the east by a line sent out: above the set eastern border of Syria and next to Happy Arabia [Arabia Felix] as far as the section which has degrees 70 30 $1/2$. Next to the desert indeed of Arabia it stretches over the remaining line. Mountains are extended indeed in the region which are called the Melani or Black, namely from the gulf [onwards]; the Saraceni are from the west of these mountains near Egypt, then there is a certain assembly under which in the gulf itself are the Phanaritae. Next to the mountains of Happy Arabia [are] the Ratheni.

### THE SITUATION OF MESOPOTAMIA
MESOPOTAMIA is bounded on the north by the described part of Greater Armenia. On the west by the noted part of the Euphrates river near Syria. On the east by the part of the Tigris river near Assyria, that is, from the section which is near Armenia as far as the Altars of Hercules, which has 80 34 2/3 degrees. On the south by the remaining part of the Euphrates near Desert Arabia as far as its boundary, which has 76 1/4 33 1/3 degrees; and near Babylonia as far as it meets the Tigris river and as far as the aforementioned altars; the degrees of this section are 80 34 1/3.

#### Famous mountains in Mesopotamia are:
Mount Casius, the middle of which has 74 37 1/3 degrees. And Mount Singaris, 76 1/3 36 1/4.
Many rivers run through the region from the said mountains, and that which is called Chaboras, the source of which has 74 37 1/4 degrees; its junction with the Euphrates has 72 39 degrees. And that which is called Saocoras, the sources of which are 79 37 1/2; and its junction with the Euphrates is 76 34. Anthemusia occupies the region near Armenia, above which is Chalcitis, and below which is Gauzanitis, and Acabena is by the Tigris river. Below Gauzanitis is Ingena, and far along the Euphrates is Ancobaritis.

### THE SITUATION OF THE BABYLONIAN REGION
BABYLONIA is bounded on the north by Mesopotamia near the described part of the Euphrates river; on the west by Desert Arabia near the aforesaid mountains; on the east by Susiana near the remaining part of the Tigris river as far as its mouths in the Persian Gulf, which have 80 31 degrees. Adjacent to the Euphrates is the region of Achanitis. Adjacent to Desert Arabia is the region of Chaldea. Around the marshes are the Mardoceni; below you have those called Strophades. ### THE SITUATION OF ASSYRIA
ASSYRIA IS BOUNDED on the north by the aforesaid part of Armenia near Mount Niphates; on the west by Mesopotamia near the described boundary of the Tigris river. On the south by Susiana along a line from the Tigris river which is below the Altars of Hercules through degrees 80 1/2 34 1/2 as far as the boundary 84 36. On the east by a part of Media along a line joining from there to the boundary of Armenia above which is Mount Coatthras, whose boundaries are 80 39 2/3 and 83 38. The part of the region which is near Armenia is called Arrapachitis. That which is near Susiana is Sittacene. The Garramei occupy the middle. That which is between Arrapachitis and the Garamei is called Adiabena. That which is between the Garamei and Sittacene is Apolloniatis, above which lies the Sabiate tribe. And above Adiabena is Calacena. The region of Arbilitis hangs over the Garamei. Rivers run through the region, mixing themselves into the Tigris river: the Lycus, whose sources are 78 39, and the mixture with the Tigris 79 36 1/2. And the river Caprus, whose sources are 79 39 1/2, and the mixture with the Tigris 79 1/2 36 1/12. And the Gorgus, whose sources are 80 1/3 38, and the mixture at the Tigris 80 34 1/3.

### THE DESCRIPTION OF SUSIANA
SUSIANA is bounded on the north by Assyria along its described side; on the west by Babylonia along the described part of the Tigris as far as the sea; on the east by Persis along a line extending from the aforesaid boundary near Assyria and the Medes as far as the mouths in the Persian sea of the river Oroatis. On the south by the part of the Persian Gulf which pertains from this river as far as the Tigris river according to this description. After the eastern mouths of the Tigris:

### THE SITUATION OF PERSIS
PERSIS is bounded on the north by the Medes along the line described through Mount Parchoatras. On the west by Susiana along the said eastern side. On the east by the two Carmanias along a southern line produced from the boundary near Media and Parthia as far as the mouths of the Bagrada river which exit into the Persian Gulf at 94 29 1/2 1/4 degrees. On the south by the part of the Persian Gulf from the mouths of the river Oroandis [Oroatis] as far as the river Bagrada according to this description.

### THE SITUATION OF DESERT CARMANIA
Desert CARMANIA is bounded on the west by a part of Persis near the river Bagrada which extends from Mount Parthoathra as far as the boundary 94 31. On the north by Parthia along the line described through Mount Parchoatra. On the east by a part of Aria along a line produced from the said line as far as the boundary 101 29 1/2 1/3. On the south by the remaining Carmania along a line joining the aforementioned limits. The Ylachite and Cuththi inhabit this desert Carmania from the southern side; in the middle are the Gadanopydres. On the north and the east, that entire side is called Modomastica.

This translation covers the provided pages from Claudius Ptolemy’s *Geographia* (often titled *Cosmographia* in the 15th century). The text spans the conclusion of Book VI and the beginning of Book VII, documenting the coordinates and regional boundaries of the Near East, Central Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.

### Scholarly Notes on the Text
*   **Abbreviations:** Common Renaissance scribal/printing abbreviations have been expanded: *vsq;* to *usque* (until/as far as), *ff* to *fluvii* (of the river), *q̄* to *quod* or *que* (which/that), and *p̄fatus* to *praefatus* (aforesaid).
*   **Proper Nouns:** As requested, names of cities, tribes, and rivers are maintained in their Latin forms (e.g., *Oxa* for Oxus, *Iaxartes* for Jaxartes).
*   **Coordinates:** Longitude and latitude are provided in degrees and fractions thereof, following the Ptolemaic 360-degree system.

### LOCATION OF MARGIANA
**MARGIANA** is bounded on the west by Hyrcania along the side already set forth. On the north by a part of Scythia which extends from the mouths of the river Oxa as far as the section which is near Bactriana, the degree of which is 103 44. On the south by a part of Aria along an equidistant line which starts from the border marked near Hyrcania and Parthia, passing through the Sariphos mountains as far as the end, the position of which is 109 39. On the east by Bactriana along the mountains which join the aforementioned borders.

### LOCATION OF BACTRIANA
**BACTRIANA** has as its boundaries on the west Margiana along the side set forth. On the north and the rising of the sun [east], the Sogdiani along the remaining part of the river Oxa. On the south by a part of Aria which extends from the border which is near Margiana as far as the border [at] 111 39. Moreover, the rivers Oxa flow through the region, joining themselves [with] the Ocus, whose sources have degrees 110 39. And the Dargamanis, whose sources are 116 36 $1/3$. And the Zatrapsis, whose sources are 113 39. And the Atarmes, whose sources are 114 39. And the Dargidos, whose sources are 116 39. This indeed is mixed with the river Oxa at the position having degrees 116 $1/2$ 44. Of the rest, the Atarmes and Zariaspae, having first been mixed with each other at position 113 40, are mixed into the Oxa at degrees 112 $1/2$ 44. The Dargamanis and Ochus, themselves also having first been mixed together at degrees 109 40 $1/6$, go out into the Oxa at degrees 109 44 $1/3$. The location of Mount Paropanisus is 111 $1/2$ 39 and 119 $1/2$ 39. In Bactriana, those parts which are northern near the river are held by the Salatere and Zariaspe; south of these, below the Salatere, are the Comari, below whom are the Chomi. Afterward the Acyanace; afterward the Tambizi. Below the Zariaspe indeed are the Thocari, a great tribe, below whom are the Marinei and Sconde and Varni, and also below them the Sabadij. Below the Sabadij are the Orfiti and Anares.

### LOCATION OF THE SOGDIANI
**SOGDIANI** are bounded on the west by a part of Scythia which extends from the section of the river Oxa through the Oxian mountains near Bactriana and Margiana as far as the section of the river Iaxartes, which has degrees 110 49. On the north likewise by a part of Scythia along the section therefrom of the river Iaxartes as far as the end of its bend, the degrees of which are 120 48 $1/2$. On the east sufficiently near the bend from there of the Iaxartes as far as its sources, which have degrees 125 43. And along a line produced from these as far as 125 38 $1/2$. On the south also and the west [by] Bactriana along the set forth section of the Oxa and the mountains which are specifically called the Caucasus, along the line joining the aforementioned end and the sources of the Oxa, which have 125 38. Moreover, the mountains extend...

### LOCATION OF THE SACAE
**THE SACAE** are bounded on the west by the Sogdiani along their set forth eastern side; on the north by Scythia along an equidistant line which is drawn from the bend of the river Iaxartes as far as the end, the position of which is 130 49. On the east likewise by Scythia along lines produced therefrom through the mountain called Ascatancas as far as the garrison or town of those who set out to the Seres at the foot of Mount Imaus, of which town the degrees are 140 43. And through Mount Imaus turning toward the north as far as the end which has degrees 140 35. On the south by Mount Imaus itself along the line joining the aforementioned borders. The region of the Sacae is one of nomads; for it does not have cities, but inhabits groves and caves. Moreover, in it are the aforesaid Comedorum mountains, the ascent of which from the Sogdiani has 125 43 degrees. Those indeed which are near the valley of the Comedi have degrees 130 35. And the tower which is called the Stone Tower [Turris Lapidea] has degrees 135 43. Those who are near the Iaxartes are called the Carate and Comari. Those who are above the mountains are all the Comede. Those near Ascatanca are the Massagete. Those who lie between are the Grunei Scythians and Toorne, below whom near Mount Imaus are the Bylte.

### LOCATION OF SCYTHIA WITHIN MOUNT IMAUS
**SCYTHIA within Mount Imaus** is bounded on the west by Asiatic Sarmatia according to the line set forth. On the north by unknown land [terra incognita]. On the east by Mount Imaus turning toward the north according to a nearly meridian line which extends from the aforementioned town as far as the unknown land. On the south and also the east sufficiently indeed both by the Sogdiani and Margiana along their set forth lines as far as the mouths of the river Oxa emptying into the Hyrcanian Sea and also by the part which is from here as far as the mouths of the river Rha, which has degrees 87 $2/3$ 48 $2/3$ $1/12$. It turns toward the west at degrees 85 54 $1/4$.

**The mountains surround the Seres:**
Those which are called the Annibi, whose ends have 153 60 & 171 56. And the western part of the Auzacian [mountains] which was mentioned. And a part of the Casian mountains, even the eastern part as has been set forth. Likewise also the eastern parts of the Emodus mountains which are called the Seric [mountains] as has also been said. And the Asmirei mountains whose ends have degrees 167 47 $1/2$ & 174 47 $1/2$. And Mount Tagurus, the middle of which is 170 43. And that which is called Mount Otthorocoras, whose ends are 169 36 & 174 39. Two rivers especially run through the region, the Oechardes rivers whose source near the Auzacians has been mentioned. Indeed, the source which is near the Asmirei mountains has degrees 174 47 $1/2$. The division indeed near the Casian mountains has almost degrees 160 49 $1/2$. Moreover, the fork which is there twice is 161 44 $3/4$. The parts of Serica which are most northern are inhabited by the tribe of the Antropophagi [Cannibals], below whom are the Annibi tribe which dwells near the mountains of the same name. Between these and the Ausatians are the Siriges, below whom... after the Piale even to the river Oechardes and under this the Oecharde of the same name. Also that which is called the river Bautisus, whose source indeed which is at the Casian mountains has degrees 160 43. That indeed which is at the Ottocara is 176 39. The division indeed at the Emodus is 168 39. The source indeed which is twice there is 160 37. Again, further east than the rivers are the Garinei and Rhabbanti, below whom twice is the Asmiraea region above the mountains of the same name. ### LOCATION OF ARIA
**ARIA** is bounded on the north by Margiana and a part of Bactriana along their set forth southern lines. On the west by Parthia and Carmania Deserta along their noted eastern lines. On the south by Drangiana along a line beginning from the aforementioned end near Carmania and turning toward the north through Mount Bagous, it turns to the east even to the end, the degrees of which are 111 34. Moreover, the position of the mountain bend has degrees 109 32. On the east by the Paropanisadae along a meridian line joining the set forth ends through the western parts of the Paropanisus. Moreover, the position of the Paropanisus is near three signs of which the northern one is 111 $1/2$ 39. That which is southern is 111 36. That which is furthest east is 119 $1/2$ 39. Moreover, the famous river Arius divides the region, the sources of which indeed in the Paropanisadae are 111 36 $1/4$. Those indeed near the Sariphi [mountains] are 103 38 $2/3$. The part indeed near the lake made by it and called Aria itself has degrees 108 $2/3$ 36. In Aria, the northern parts are held by the Nesei and Astaueni. Those indeed near Parthia and Carmania Deserta are the Masdorani. Those indeed [near] Drangiana are the Cesitote. Those near the Paropanisadae are the Paurati, below whom are the Obares. The part indeed which lies between is held by the Dracheme, below whom are the Etimadri.

The "Camel-Herders" <note>original: "Camelobosci"</note> called the Sozote hold the areas near the deserts. Below these, far from the sea, extend the Rhudiana and Agdenitis regions; then the Parepaphitis, below which are the Are and Charadre peoples. Next are Cabadena and Cathonina, and above the sea are the Pasargade and the "Tortoise-Eaters" <note>original: "Celonophagi"</note>. The inland cities and villages in Carmania are said to be these:

### THE SITUATION OF MARGIANA
**MARGIANA** is bounded on the west by Hyrcania along the side already described. On the north by a part of Scythia which extends from the mouths of the Oxus River <note>original: "Oxe amnis"</note> as far as the division that is near Bactriana, which is at 103° 44'. On the south by a part of Aria along the parallel line which goes from the boundary noted near Hyrcania and Parthia through the Sariphi mountains as far as the end, the position of which is 109° 39'. On the east by Bactriana along the mountainous regions which join the aforementioned boundaries.

### THE LOCATION OF BACTRIANA
**BACTRIANA** is bounded on the west by Margiana along the side already described. On the north and towards the rising sun <note>the East</note> by the Sogdians, along the remaining part of the Oxus River <note>modern Amu Darya</note>. On the south by the part of Aria which extends from the border near Margiana as far as the end point at 111° 39'. The rivers flowing through the region and joining the Oxus are: the Ochus, whose sources are at 110° 39'; the Dargamanis, whose sources are at 116° 36 1/3'; the Zatrapsis, whose sources are at 113° 39'; the Atarmes, whose sources are at 114° 39'; and the Dargidos, whose sources are at 116° 39'. This last river joins the Oxus River at the location of 116 1/2° 44'. As for the others, the Atarmes and the Zariaspae <note>original: "zariaspae"</note> first mix with each other at 113° 40' and then join the Oxus at 112 1/2° 44'. The Dargamanis and the Ochus also mix together at 109° 40 1/6' and flow out into the Oxus at 109° 44 1/3'. The location of the Paropanisus Mountain <note>the Hindu Kush range</note> is 111 1/2° 39' and 119 1/2° 39'. In the northern parts of Bactriana near the river, the Salatere and Zariaspe tribes dwell. South of the Salatere are the Comari, below whom are the Chomi. Then the Acyanace, and then the Tambizi. Below the Zariaspe is the great nation of the Tochari <note>original: "Thocari magnū genus"</note>, below whom are the Marinei, the Sconde, and the Varni, and even below them, the Sabadii. Below the Sabadii are the Orfiti and the Anares.

**THE SOGDIANS** are bounded on the west by a part of Scythia which extends from the section of the Oxus River through the Oxian mountains near Bactriana and Margiana as far as the section of the Jaxartes River <note>modern Syr Darya</note> located at 110° 49'. On the north, likewise by a part of Scythia from the section of the Jaxartes River to the end of its bend at 120° 48 1/2'. On the east by the bend of the Jaxartes as far as its sources at 125° 43', and along a line drawn from there to 125° 38 1/2'. On the south and west by Bactriana, along the described section of the Oxus and the mountains properly called the Caucasus <note>not the modern Caucasus, but refers here to the eastern extensions of the Hindu Kush</note>, following the line joining the aforementioned border and the sources of the Oxus at 125° 38'. ...[joining] almost between the two rivers which are called the Sogdian <note>original: "fluuios qui Sogdij dicuntur"; though the text says "rivers," this likely refers to the Sogdian mountain range which lies between the Oxus and Jaxartes rivers</note>, whose boundaries have the coordinates 111° 47' and 122° 44 1/2'. East of these are the Drespiani, who occupy the area joining both rivers. Further east than these are the Anieses near the Jaxartes, and the Chirrodees near the Oxus. And between the Caucasian Mountains and the Imaus is the region named Vandabanda.

### THE LOCATION OF THE SACHAE
**THE SACHAE** <note>original: "SACHAE"; the Sakas, a group of nomadic Iranian peoples</note> are bounded on the west by the Sogdians along their eastern side already described; on the north by Scythia along a parallel line drawn from the bend of the Jaxartes river to the end point at 130° 49'. On the east likewise by Scythia along lines produced from there through the mountain called Ascatancas to the fortress or town of those who set out for the land of the Seres <note>The Seres were the people of ancient China, known to the West through the silk trade</note> near the Imaus mountain, which town is at 140° 43'. And through the Imaus mountain turning towards the north to the end point at 140° 35'. On the south by the Imaus mountain itself along the line joining the aforementioned boundaries. The region of the Sachae is one of nomads, for it has no cities; they inhabit forests and caves. There are also in it the aforementioned mountains of the Comedi, whose ascent from the Sogdians is at 125° 43'. Those things near the valley of the Comedi are at 130° 35'. And the tower which is called the Stone Tower <note>original: "turris... lapidea"; a famous landmark on the Silk Road, likely the station where Western traders met those from the East</note> is at 135° 43'. Those near the Jaxartes are called the Caratae and the Comari. Those above the mountains are all called Comedi. Those near the Ascatanca are the Massagetae. Those who lie in between are the Grunaei Scythians and the Toornae; below whom, near the Imaus mountain, are the Byltae.

### THE LOCATION OF SCYTHIA WITHIN THE IMAUS MOUNTAIN
**SCYTHIA** within the Imaus mountain range is bounded on the west by Asiatic Sarmatia according to the line already set forth; on the north by unknown land. On the east by the Imaus mountain turning towards the north according to a nearly meridian line that extends from the aforementioned town to the unknown land. On the south and also the east by the Sachae <note>original: "Satis"; likely a clerical error for "Sachis"</note> and the Sogdians and Margiana along the lines described for them as far as the mouth of the Oxus river flowing out into the Hyrcanian Sea <note>The Caspian Sea</note>, and also the part extending from here to the mouth of the Rha River <note>The Volga River</note>, which is at 87 2/3° 48 2/3 1/12'. To the west, it turns at 85° 54 1/4'.

After the mouths of the Oxus <note>Coordinates for the Oxus river mouth: 100° 43'</note>.
The notable mountains of Scythia within the Imaus range are more to the east and are called the **Alani**, whose boundaries are at 105° 52 ½' and 118° 52 ½'. And those called the **Rhymmici**, whose boundaries are at 90° 54' and 99° 57 ¼'. From these flow the Rhymmus and certain other rivers into the Rha river <note>The Rha is the ancient name for the Volga</note> and those joining the Daix river. And the **Norossus** mountain, whose boundaries are at 97° 53' and 106° 52 ½'. From this mountain flows the Daix river, and certain others mixing into the Jaxartes river. And the mountains which are called the **Aspesii**, whose extreme points have the coordinates 111° 55 ½' and 117° 52 ½'. And from these, some rivers flow to the Jaxartes river. And the **Tapuri** mountains, whose boundaries are 120° 56' and 125° 45'. From which again certain rivers run out to the Jaxartes. Among these, between the rivers and the Imaus mountain, rise the **Sichi** <note>Also known as the Syebi</note>, whose boundaries have the coordinates 121° 58' and 132° 62'. And those called the **Amarei** mountains, whose boundaries have the coordinates 130° 56' and 137° 50'. After these is the bend of the Imaus mountain turning toward the north. All this part of Scythia toward the north, near the unknown land, is inhabited by those who are collectively called the **Alan Scythians**, and the **Suobeni**, and the **Alanorsi**. In the part which is below these, the **Setyani**, the **Messei**, and the **Sychi** hold the land, and near the Imaus mountain, the **Tectosaces**. Near the more eastern sources of the Rha river are the **Rhobofci**, below whom are the **Acmani**. Then the **Paniardi**, below whom, now by the river, is the region of **Canodipsa**, and below that the **Coraxi**. After them the **Orgasi**, after whom is the great race of the **Iaxartae** near the river of the same name, extending to the bend toward the Tapurian mountains. Again, below the Setyani are the **Malogeni**; below whom, reaching as far as the Rhymmic mountains, are the **Samnitae**; below the Messei and the Alan mountains are the **Zaratae** and the **Salones**; and those further east than the Rhymmic mountains are the **Tybiacae**. After them are the **Tibizaretis**, the **Tabieni**, the **Iasce**, and the **Machetegi** near the Norossus mountain, below whom are the **Norosbes** and the **Norossi**, and below these the **Catage Scythians** near the Jaxartes. Furthermore, more to the west of the Aspesian mountains are the **Aspesii Scythians**, while more to the east are the **Galactophagi** <note>Greek: "Milk-eaters"; a common name for nomadic tribes in antiquity</note>. Similarly, east of the Tapurian mountains and the Syebi are the **Tapurei**; and those near the Amarei mountains and the Ascatancas mountain are the Scythians of the same name. The **Anarei** indeed are below the Tectosaces. The **Ascatancae** are further east than the Tapurian mountains and inhabit the area as far as the Imaus mountain. Between the Oxian mountains and the section at the mouths of the Jaxartes, and the coastal areas lying between the two rivers, the **Arite** hold the land near the Jaxartes, and below them the **Namaste**. Then the **Sagarauce**, and near the Oxus river, the **Rhibii**. In which area is the city:

### THE LOCATION OF SCYTHIA BEYOND THE IMAVS MOUNTAIN
**BEYOND** the Imaus mountain, Scythia is bounded on the west by Interior Scythia and the Sacae along the whole diversion of the mountains toward the north. To the north by the unknown land. To the east by Seris <note>The land of the Seres, or China</note> according to a straight line whose boundaries have the coordinates 150° 63' and 155° 35'. To the south by the part of India that is beyond the Ganges river, along a line equidistant to the previously set boundaries. In this portion lies the western part of the **Auzacian** mountains, whose boundaries are 149° and 165° 57'. And part of the mountains called **Casius**, also turning toward the west, whose boundaries have the coordinates 153° 40' and 157° 44'. Near the Auzacians is the source of the Oechardus river, which is at 153° 52'. This Scythia is inhabited to the north by the **Abii Scythians**; below them are the **Hippophagi Scythians** <note>Greek: "Horse-eaters"</note>; after whom the region of **Auzacitis** extends; and below this, near the aforementioned town, is the **Cassian** region. Below that are the **Cathe Scythians**; then the **Achasa** region; and below this, near the Emodi mountains <note>Often identified with the Himalayas</note>, the **Curanei Scythians**.

Also the **Asmiraean** mountains, whose limits are at 167° 47 ½' and 174° 47 ½'. And Mount **Tagurus**, the middle of which is at 170° 43'. The source which is twice there is 160° 37'. Again, further east than the rivers are the **Garinaei** and the **Rhabannae**; below which is the region of **Asmiraea**, above the mountains of the same name. Below these, as far as the Casius mountains, are the **Issedones**, a great nation, and to their east the **Throani**. Below these are the **Taguri** on the eastern side of the mountain of the same name. Below the Issedones are the **Aspetatae**, and below them the **Batae**, and the southernmost near the Emodus and Seric mountains are the **Ottorocorae**.

### THE LOCATION OF ARIA
**ARIA** <note>Aria corresponds to the region around Herat in modern Afghanistan</note> is bounded on the north by **Margiana** and part of **Bactriana** along their established southern lines. On the west by **Parthia** and the desert of **Carmania** along their noted eastern lines. On the south by **Drangiana** along a line beginning from the aforementioned limit near Carmania; and bending northward through Mount **Bagous**, it turns to the east as far as the limit at 111° 34'. The location of the mountain's bend is at 109° 32'. On the east by the **Paropanisadae** <note>The region of the Hindu Kush</note> along the southern line joining the established limits through the western parts of Paropanisus. The location of Paropanisus is according to three marks, of which the northern is 111 ½° 39', the southern 111° 36', and the most eastern 119 ½° 39'. A notable river, the **Arius**, divides the region; its sources which are in the Paropanisadae are at 111° 36 ¼'. Those near the **Sariphi** are at 103° 38 ⅔'. The part near the lake formed by it is also called Aria, and is at 108 ⅔° 36'. In Aria, the **Nesei** and **Astaveni** hold the northern parts. Those near Parthia and the Carmanian desert are the **Masdorani**. Those near Drangiana are the **Caesitote**. Those near the Paropanisadae are the **Paurati**, below whom are the **Obares**. Those lying between are held by the **Dracheme**, below whom are the **Etimadri**.

### THE SITUATION OF PAROPANISUS
**THE PAROPANISADAE** <note>A region centered on the Hindu Kush mountains, spanning eastern Afghanistan and northern Pakistan</note> are bounded to the west by Aria near the previously mentioned side. To the north, they are bounded by a part of Bactria. To the east, they are bounded by a part of India along a southern line drawn from the sources of the Oxus River through the Caucasian mountains <note>The 'Caucasus' here refers to the *Caucasus Indicus*, or Hindu Kush, which Alexander's army named after the European Caucasus</note> as far as the end, the coordinates of which are 119° 32 2/3'. And to the south, they are bounded by Arachosia along a line which joins the established boundaries through the Paureti mountains. Furthermore, the Dargamanis river, located in the direction of Bactria, is received into the region, its position being 116 1/2° 39 2/3'. Also the river Choe <note>Likely the Kabul River or one of its tributaries</note>, joining it, the sources of which have the coordinates 115° 34 1/2'. The northern parts of the region are held by the Bolitae. The western parts by the Aristophili. The eastern parts by the Ambautae. The southern parts by the Paroetae, and below these the Parii.

### THE SITUATION OF DRANGIANA
**DRANGIANA** <note>The ancient region of Sistan, located in southwestern Afghanistan and southeastern Iran</note> is bounded to the west and north by Aria along the line set forth coming out of Mount Bagous. To the east, it is bounded by Arachosia along the southern line drawn from its boundary among the Arii and Paropanisadae as far as the limit at 111 1/2° 28'. To the south, it is bounded by part of Gedrosia along the line joining the established boundaries through the Betian mountains. A river cut off from the Arabis <note>The Arabis is the modern Hab River; Ptolemy describes a branch of it dividing this region</note> divides the region, the coordinates of which are 109° 32 1/2'. Near Aria, the Darandae hold the land; near Arachosia, the Batrii. The part that lies between them is called Tarracena.

### THE SITUATION OF ARACHOSIA
**ARACHOSIA** <note>original: "ARACHOSIA"; an ancient satrapy of the Achaemenid and Seleucid Empires, centered on modern Kandahar, Afghanistan</note> is bounded on the west by Drangiana and on the north by the region of the Paropanisadae along the sides already described. To the east, it is bounded by a part of India along a southern line extending from the border of the Paropanisadae to the point whose coordinates are 119° 28'. To the south, it is bounded by the remaining part of Gedrosia along a line joining the described borders through the Betius mountain range. Moreover, a river is received into this region, diverted from the Indus <note>The Indus is one of the longest rivers in Asia, the "backbone" of ancient Indian geography</note>, the sources of which are at 114° 32 1/2'. The diversion point is at 122 1/2° 27 1/2'. Those who occupy the northern parts of the region are called the Pargietae. Below them are the Sydri, followed by the Roplutae and the Eoritae.

### THE SITUATION OF GEDROSIA
**GEDROSIA** <note>A dry, mountainous coastal region along the Arabian Sea, modern Baluchistan in Pakistan and Iran</note> is bounded on the west by Carmania along the southern line described as far as the sea. To the north, it is bounded by Drangiana and Arachosia along their noted southern lines. To the east, it is bounded by a part of India along the Indus river by a line extending from the border of Arachosia to the terminus that reaches the sea, the coordinates of which are 109° 20 3/4'. To the south, it is bounded by a part of the Indian Sea <note>The Arabian Sea</note>, the description of which is as follows, after the border that is near Carmania:

| Landmark | Longitude | Latitude |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| Mouths of the river Arabis <note>Modern Hab River</note> | 105 | 20 1/4 |

| The split of the river entering Drangiana | 107 2/3 | 25 |
| The city of Rhagiana | 106 | 20 |
| Port of the Women <note>original: "Mulierum portus"</note> | 107 | 20 |
| Cosamba | 108 | 20 |
| Phisana | 108 2/3 | 20 1/4 |

After which is the aforementioned border where it touches the sea at 109° 20'. The mountains called the Arbeti extend through the middle of Gedrosia, the ends of which are at 107° 22' and 113° 26 1/2'. From these mountains, certain streams flow and join the Indus, the source of one being at 111° 25 1/2'. Similarly, rivers flow through Gedrosia from the Betian mountains. In the part of the region near the sea, the villages of the Arbiti are located. Those near Carmania are the Parisini. Those near Arachosia are the Musateni. The entire middle of the region is called Paradene, and below it is Parisene. After these, those near the Indus are held by the Rhamnae.

### DESCRIPTION OF INDIA BEYOND THE RIVER GANGES.

**INDIA BEYOND** the Ganges is bounded on the west by the river Ganges; on the north by the described parts of Scythia and Serica; on the east by the region of the Sinae [Chinese] along a meridian line sent from the end of Serica as far as the gulf called the Great [Gulf], and by that gulf itself; on the south by the Indian Sea and part of the Prassodan sea which extends from the island of Menuthias through a parallel line as far as the opposite parts of the Great Gulf. The coastal parts of this section are arranged in this manner in the Gangetic Gulf after the mouth of the Ganges called the Antiboleus.

Between mount **Imaus** and **Bopyrrus** are the **Tacorei**, turning mostly toward the north [Arctos]; the **Corancoli** are below them. After that the **Passalae**. After which above the **Meandrus** are the **Tilebae**, but they call them **Besadae**. For they are mutilated [or stunted]: thick and broader in the forehead: white in color. Above **Cirradia**, in which they say the best *malabathrum* is made, the **Tamene Anthropophagi** [man-eaters] inhabit near the mountain **Meandrus**. Above the Silver region, in which many imperfect [native] metals are said to be, is situated the Golden region, closest to the **Besingiti**, and this has more gold mines than many others.
