# THE NINTH MAP OF ASIA

**T**HE NINTH MAP OF ASIA contains Aria, the Paropanisadae, Drangiana, Arachosia, and Gedrosia. <note>These ancient regions correspond to central and southern Afghanistan, eastern Iran, and the Makran coast of Pakistan.</note> Its central parallel has a proportion to the meridian of thirteen to fifteen. This map is bounded on the east by India; on the south by the Indian Sea; on the west by both Carmania and Parthia; and on the north by Margiana and Bactriana.

### NOTABLE CITIES OF ARIA
**Aria** has a maximum day of 14 and 3/4 hours <note>Original: 14 2/3 1/12</note> and is distant from Alexandria <note>Ptolemy uses Alexandria, Egypt, as his prime meridian for calculating time differences.</note> toward the east by 3 hours.
**Bitaxa** has a maximum day of 14 and 2/3 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 3 and 3/4 hours <note>Original: 3 2/3 1/12</note>.
**Alexandria of Aria** <note>Modern Herat, Afghanistan.</note> has a maximum day of 14 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 3 and 1/2 hours.

### NOTABLE CITIES OF THE PAROPANISADAE
<note>The Paropanisadae were the people living at the base of the Hindu Kush mountains.</note>
**Naulibis** has a maximum day of 14 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 3 and 1/2 hours.
**Carura**, also known as Orcospana, has a maximum day of 14 and 5/12 hours <note>Original: 14 1/3 1/12</note> and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by [3 and 1/2] hours. <note>The hour count is cut off in the source but follows the previous entry.</note>

### NOTABLE CITIES OF DRANGIANA
<note>Drangiana is the historical region of Sistan.</note>
**Prothasia** has a maximum day of 14 and 1/6 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 3 and 1/6 hours.
**Ariaspa** has a maximum day of 13 and 2/3 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 3 and 1/4 hours.

### NOTABLE CITIES OF ARACHOSIA
<note>Arachosia centers around modern-day Kandahar, Afghanistan.</note>
**Alexandria** <note>Likely Alexandria in Arachosia, modern Kandahar.</note> has a maximum day of 14 and 1/12 hours and is distant from Alexandria [in Egypt] toward the east by 3 and 1/10 hours.
**Archotus** has a maximum day of 14 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 3 and 3/10 hours.

### NOTABLE CITIES OF GEDROSIA
<note>Gedrosia is the coastal desert region of modern-day Balochistan.</note>
**Cuni** has a maximum day of nearly 13 and 2/3 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 3 and 1/3 hours.
**Mularna** has a maximum day of 13 and 3/4 hours <note>Original: 13 1/2 1/4</note> and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 3 and 2/3 hours.
**Arbis** has a maximum day of nearly 13 and 1/2 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 3 hours.

Here also the sun is directly overhead once a year at the summer tropic <note>The Tropic of Cancer</note>. We say this because the sun is near the tropic itself. However, it should be known that it is distant by one-third of a "great degree"—which, in a system of 30 divisions of the zodiac, results in three degrees. Here, the sun must necessarily be directly overhead not just once a year, but twice: specifically, when it is three degrees away from the summer tropic on either side, just as is written for other cities located at the same latitude.

# THE TENTH MAP OF ASIA

**T**HE TENTH MAP OF ASIA contains India within the Ganges <note>Original: India intra Gangem; referring to the Indian subcontinent west of the Ganges river</note> together with its adjacent islands. Its middle parallel <note>A line of latitude used as a reference point for the map's scale</note> has a proportion to the meridian of eleven to twelve. The map is bounded:
On the East, by India beyond the Ganges <note>Original: India extra Gangem; referring to Southeast Asia</note>.
On the South, by the Gangetic part of the Indian Sea <note>The Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean</note>.
On the West, by Gedrosia, Arachosia, and the Paropanisadae <note>Regions corresponding to modern-day Balochistan, southern Afghanistan, and the Hindu Kush</note>.
On the North, by that part of Mount Imaus <note>The Himalayas and associated ranges</note> which lies below the Sogdians and the Sacae.

**Symilla** <note>Likely modern Chaul, near Mumbai</note> has its longest day of nearly 12 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/12 hours <note>This equals 12 hours and 55 minutes</note> and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 3 1/3 hours. Here also the sun is twice a year directly overhead <note>Original: supra verticem; at the zenith</note> when it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 41 3/4 degrees.

**Muzoris** <note>Muziris, a famous ancient port, likely modern Kodungallur</note> has its longest day of 12 1/2 + 1/3 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 3 3/4 hours. Here also the sun is twice a year directly overhead when it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 42 1/2 + 1/4 <note>42 3/4</note> degrees.

**Chaberis** <note>Located near the mouth of the Kaveri River</note> has its longest day of 12 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/12 hours, or nearly 13, and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 4 1/2 hours. Here also the sun is twice a year directly overhead when it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 47 1/2 + 1/12 degrees.

**Palura** <note>A port on the Bay of Bengal</note> has its longest day of 12 2/3 + 1/10 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 4 2/3 hours. Here also the sun is twice a year directly overhead when it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 7 1/4 degrees <note>This degree value appears low compared to the previous entries, suggesting a potential scribal error in the degree count or a misunderstanding of the latitude</note>.

**Caspira** <note>Kashmir</note> has its longest day of nearly 14 1/2 <note>OCR reads "14 12"; interpreted as 14 1/2 based on Ptolemaic tradition</note> hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by nearly 4 1/2 hours.

**Bucephala** <note>A city founded by Alexander the Great on the Jhelum River</note> has its longest day of 14 1/4 hours <note>OCR reads "11 1/4", but geographical context and Ptolemaic tables suggest 14 1/4</note> and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 4 1/3 + 3/30 hours.

### PAGE 1

The ELEVENTH map of Asia contains **India** beyond the **Ganges** and the **Sinae**. Its middle parallel has almost the same proportion [to the meridian] as the meridian. The map is bounded: From the East by unknown land. From the South by part of the **Gangetic** gulf, the **Indian** sea, the Great Gulf, and also by unknown land. From the West by **India** within the **Ganges**. From the North by part of **Scythia** and the **Seres**.

**CITIES OF OUTER INDIA**
**Tacola** has a longest day of 12 1/4 equinoctial hours and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by 6 1/3 [hours]. Here the sun becomes directly overhead twice in the year, being distant from the summer tropic on either side by 79 1/2 degrees. [Note: *usus* in the OCR is a likely error for *versus* (toward)].
**Zabe** has a longest day of 12 1/4 hours and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by 7 1/3 hours. Here the sun becomes directly overhead twice in the year, being distant from the summer tropic on either side by 78 2/4 degrees.
**Tosala** has a longest day of 13 1/2 hours and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by 6 1/4 hours. Here the sun becomes directly overhead once in the year, at the summer tropic itself.
**Soagma** has a longest day of 13 1/4 hours and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by 6 1/8 hours. Here the sun becomes directly overhead twice in the year, being distant from the summer tropic on either side by 14 degrees.
**Trilingum** has a longest day of 13 hours and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by 6 1/4 hours. Here the sun becomes directly overhead twice in the year, being distant from the summer tropic on either side by 39 degrees.
**Mareura** has a longest day of 12 1/2 1/4 [12 hours 45 min] hours and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by almost 6 1/2 hours.

**NOTABLE CITIES OF THE SINAE**
**Aspitra** has a longest day of 13 1/8 hours and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by 7 3/4 hours. Here the sun becomes directly overhead twice in the year, being distant from the summer tropic on either side by 49 2/4 degrees.
**Tine** metropolis has a longest day of 13 1/8 hours and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by 8 hours. Here the sun becomes directly overhead twice in the year, being distant from the summer tropic on either side by 43 1/8 degrees.
**Cattigara** station has a longest day of 12 1/2 hours and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by 7 2/4 hours, with the southern pole raised above the earth. Here the sun becomes directly overhead twice in the year, being distant from the summer tropic on either side by 68 2/4 degrees.
**Delta abadei** island, where the metropolis named **Argentea** [Silver] has a longest day of 12 1/2 hours, similarly with the southern pole raised above the earth, and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by 7 1/3 hours. Here the sun becomes directly overhead twice in the year, being distant from the summer tropic on either side by 68 2/4 degrees.

### PAGE 2

THE TWELFTH and final map of Asia contains the island of **Taprobane** with the other adjacent islands. Its middle parallel has the same proportion to the meridian. The map is bounded on all sides by the **Indian** sea.

**NOTABLE CITIES OF TAPROBANE**
**Talacoris** emporium has a longest day of 11 3/4 equinoctial hours and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by 4 1/2 1/4 [4 hours 45 min] hours.
**Agabida** has a longest day of 12 1/2 hours and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by 4 1/2 1/4 hours. Here the sun becomes directly overhead twice in the year when it is distant from the summer tropic on either side by 69 2/4 degrees.
**Maagrammum** metropolis has a longest day of 12 1/2 1/2 [13] hours and is distant from **Alexandria** toward the East by 4 1/3 1/2 [4 hours 50 min] hours. Here the sun becomes directly overhead twice in the year when it is distant from the summer tropic on either side by 72 2/4 degrees.

THE TWELVE MAPS OF GREATER ASIA END SUCCESSFULLY.

All our provinces of the habitable [world] are ninety-four.

For whatever peoples lie beneath the zodiac, the sun becomes directly overhead twice as it descends from the north to the south, and similarly twice as it ascends; thus, what occurs once a year for others, occurs twice for them. All those, moreover, who dwell beneath the zodiac from the west to the east are **Ethyopes**, being similarly black in color; and those especially who are under the equinoctial circle [equator] become abundantly black. Those, however, who dwell outside the perpendicular line [cathetus] of the zodiac are lighter in color and tend toward whiteness according to the ratio of distance, even as far as the hyperborean **Sarmatians**. The same principle applies on either side of the equinoctial toward the North and the South, as far as both poles of the zodiac.

The **ELEVENTH MAP** of Asia contains **India beyond the Ganges** <note>This refers to the regions of Southeast Asia, including the Malay Peninsula, Thailand, and Indochina.</note> and the **Sinae** <note>The Latin name for the people of China.</note>. The middle parallel of this map has almost the same proportion to the meridian as the equator. The map is bounded: On the east by unknown land. On the south by part of the Gangetic Gulf <note>The Bay of Bengal</note>, the Indian Sea, the Great Gulf <note>Likely the Gulf of Thailand or the South China Sea</note>, and also unknown land. On the west by India within the Ganges. On the north by part of Scythia and Serica <note>Regions of Central Asia and Northern China known for silk production.</note>.

### CITIES OF OUTER INDIA

**Tacola** has a longest day of 12 ¾ hours <note>original: "12 ½ ¼"</note> and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 6 ⅔ hours. Here, the sun is directly overhead twice a year, and it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 79 ⅔ degrees.

**Zabe** has a longest day of 12 ¼ hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 7 ½ hours. Here, the sun is directly overhead twice a year, and it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 78 11/12 degrees <note>original: "78 ⅔ ¼"</note>.

**Tosala** has a longest day of 13 ½ hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 6 hours. Here, the sun is directly overhead once a year, at the summer tropic itself.

**Soagma** has a longest day of 13 ¼ hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 6 ⅛ hours. Here, the sun is directly overhead twice a year, and it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 14 degrees.

**Trilingum** has a longest day of 13 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 6 ¼ hours.

<column-break/>

Here, the sun is directly overhead twice a year, and it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 39 degrees.

**Mareura** has a longest day of 12 ¾ hours <note>original: "12 ½ ¼"</note> and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by almost 6 ½ hours.

### NOTABLE CITIES OF THE SINAE

**Aspitra** has a longest day of 13 ⅛ hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 7 ⅔ hours. Here, the sun is directly overhead twice a year, and it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 49 ¾ degrees <note>original: "49 ½ ¼"</note>.

**Tine**, the capital city, has a longest day of 13 ⅛ hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 8 hours. Here, the sun is directly overhead twice a year, and it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 43 ⅛ degrees.

**Cattigara**, a trading station, has a longest day of 12 ½ hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 7 ¾ hours <note>original: "7 ½ ¼"</note>, with the **southern pole raised above the earth** <note>This indicates that Cattigara was located south of the equator, a significant detail for ancient navigators.</note>. Here, the sun is directly overhead twice a year, and it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 68 ¾ degrees.

The island of **Delta Abadei**, where there is a capital city named **Argentea** <note>meaning "Silver City"</note>, has a longest day of 12 ½ hours, similarly with the southern pole raised above the earth. It is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 7 ⅓ hours. Here, the sun is directly overhead twice a year, and it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 68 ¾ degrees.

## The twelfth and final map of Asia contains the island of Taprobane <note>original: "Taprobanā"; the ancient Greek and Roman name for the island of Sri Lanka.</note> with the other adjacent islands. ### FAMOUS CITIES OF TAPROBANE ✦

The market-town of **Talacoris** <note>An ancient port on the island of Taprobane.</note> has its longest day lasting 11 3/5 equinoctial hours <note>Standard hours of equal length, as opposed to seasonal hours which varied throughout the year.</note> and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 4 1/2 1/14 hours <note>Ptolemy measured longitudinal distance in hours of time; one hour represents 15 degrees of longitude.</note>. ✦

**Agabida** <note>An ancient settlement in Taprobane.</note> has its longest day lasting 12 1/2 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 4 1/2 1/14 hours. ✦

And here the sun is twice a year directly overhead <note>original: "supra verticem"; literally "above the crown of the head," referring to the zenith.</note> when it is distant from the summer tropic <note>The Tropic of Cancer.</note> on both sides by 69 1/2 1/4 degrees. ✦

The capital city of **Maugrammum** <note>Historically associated with the ancient Sinhalese capitals like Anuradhapura or Mahagrama.</note> has its longest day lasting 12 1/2 1/12 hours and is distant from Alexandria toward the east by 4 1/3 1/12 hours. ✦

And here the sun is twice a year directly overhead when it is distant from the summer tropic on both sides by 72 1/2 1/4 degrees. ✦

### **The First Climate**

The third parallel differs from the equator by 1/2 + 1/4 hours <note>This indicates a time difference of 45 minutes</note>, having a longest day of 12 1/2 + 1/4 hours <note>12 hours and 45 minutes</note>.

The second parallel differs from the equator by 1/2 hour, and it has a longest day of 12 and a half hours.

The first parallel differs from the equator by 1/4 hour <note>15 minutes</note>, having a longest day of 12 1/4 hours.

The Equator <note>original: "equinoctialis"</note> having a day of 12 hours continuously and always.

The first parallel toward the south differs from the equator by 1/4 hour, having a longest day of 12 and a quarter hours.

-> All the provinces of our habitable world are ninety-four ✙ <-

> ¶ For as many nations as lie beneath the zodiac <note>The tropics</note>, the sun comes to be directly overhead for them as it descends from the north to the south. Likewise, it rises for those who experience this once a year, and for others twice. Moreover, all those who live beneath the zodiac from the setting to the rising of the sun are Ethiopians <note>A general term for dark-skinned peoples in antiquity</note>; they are similarly black in color, and especially those who are directly under the equinoctial circle <note>The Equator</note> become abundantly black. Those, however, who dwell outside the perpendicular line of the zodiac are more moderate in color and tend toward whiteness according to the proportion of their distance: all the way to the Hyperborean Sarmatians <note>The far northern peoples of the Eurasian steppe</note>. The same principle applies on both sides of the equator toward the North and South, all the way to both poles of the zodiac. ⁘

# ¶ THE EIGHTH AND FINAL BOOK OF THE COSMOGRAPHY OF CLAVDIVS PTOLOMEY, MAN OF ALEXANDRIA, ENDS HERE ✙ ⁘

## ¶ THE WORK OF DONNVS NICOLAVS GERMANVS ACCORDING TO PTOLOMEY FINISHES. ✙

## ¶ IN THE YEAR 1482, ON THE SEVENTEENTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF AVGUST <note>July 16, 1482</note>. ✙

## ¶ PRINTED IN VLM BY THE INGENIOVS MAN LEONARD HOL, CITIZEN OF THE AFOREMENTIONED TOWN. ⁘
